//: Second Python DEV set (not held-out): pinned public Python applications for tuning and labelling rounds. Drift may be tuned on these repos, so their numbers are dev-set numbers.
//selection: Criteria, written down before any candidate was cloned or scanned, and before any overlap check: real, deployable Python applications (not libraries, frameworks, SDKs, tutorials, courses, templates or starters); a framework mix of Django, DRF, FastAPI, Flask and Celery, from their dependency manifests; an OSI-approved licence (permissive preferred, copyleft accepted when explicit; no source-available or modified licences); not archived, not a fork or template; default branch pushed in 2026; at least 200 parseable files (drift scan files minus parse errors, decision D3); drift census shows at least one proposal; not already a dev repo.

Discovery, 2026-11-06: GitHub repository search (gh api -X GET search/repositories) on topic:django, topic:django-rest-framework, topic:fastapi, topic:flask and topic:celery (language:Python, stars 400..40000, pushed >= 2026-08-01, size 10..400 MB), plus `repo:` lookups of well-known applications named in those results' fields or known to the selector. Metadata (licence, archived, size) from search results; sha = default-branch HEAD from git ls-remote on 2026-11-06.

19 candidates met the metadata criteria, and `node eval/study/select-holdout.mjs verify --dev` found no overlap between any of them and the primary held-out sets. They were cloned shallow at the pin and checked with drift built from main e3cf4e3 (binary sha256 151b79ddfc1a...). Dropped: 2 with fewer than 200 parseable files; 2 whose census showed no proposal; 1 that `prepare.mjs` refuses as held-out because a secondary held-out set lists it (verify then checked dev manifests only against the primary sets; it was found after the clone and scan, recorded as exposed in that set, and verify now checks the secondary sets too); and 3 with proposals but none in the default tier, of which 1 replaced the held-out one and 2 were kept out to stay within 12 repos. This list is the remaining 12.
Labelling comes later; no proposal of these repos has been labelled.

2026-11-06, in review: usaspending-api (CC0-1.0, which is not OSI-approved, so it failed the licence criterion above) was replaced by Misago (GPL-2.0). Five further OSI-licensed Django/DRF applications were found by repository search (metadata only); all five passed `verify --dev` and prepare.mjs's held-out detection before any clone, and Misago had the most proposals of the five that passed the scan and census checks.

tier.//: Rule 5's rule-kind tier, the same definition as the primary held-out sets, pre-registered here before any labelling of these repos.
